1. Core Clinical Tension: A 14-year-old immunocompetent child presents with a 4-month history of burning chest pain radiating to the shoulders, a palpable 4 cm upper sternal swelling, night sweats, and weight loss, but remains apyretic. Imaging demonstrates sternal osteolysis with soft-tissue infiltration, left-sided pulmonary condensation with mediastinal adenopathy, and intrasplenic lesions. The tension lies between a primary osseous/hematologic malignancy (such as lymphoma or Ewing sarcoma) versus an indolent multifocal infection (such as disseminated tuberculosis or pyogenic/fungal osteomyelitis).
2. Admission Breakpoint: The admission breakpoint occurs immediately prior to surgical sternal biopsy and microbiological investigations (smear microscopy, GeneXpert PCR, and mycobacterial cultures).
3. Differential Distinctions: Pyogenic bacterial osteomyelitis typically presents acutely with fever, localized erythema, and purulence rather than an indolent 4-month cold swelling with multifocal visceral involvement. Bone malignancy/lymphoma is ruled out by the absence of neoplastic architecture on biopsy and identification of Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex by GeneXpert real-time PCR and culture on MGIT and Lowenstein-Jensen media.
case_prompt:
A 14-year-old child presents with a 4-month history of burning chest pain radiating towards the shoulders, accompanied by asthenia, night sweats, and a 3-kg weight loss. One month after the onset of pain, a palpable mass appeared at the level of the upper sternum. The patient has remained apyretic. Childhood immunizations include bacille Calmette-Guérin, and there is a documented history of prior exposure to an individual with a chronic respiratory infection.

On physical examination, the patient is apyretic. A palpable swelling measuring approximately 4 cm in diameter is noted over the upper portion of the sternum. The remainder of the physical examination is unremarkable.

Initial laboratory evaluation reveals a white blood cell count of 17.6 × 10^9/L with neutrophil predominance (7.9 × 10^9/L), microcytic hypochromic anemia with hemoglobin 10.9 g/dL, and thrombocytosis with platelets 500 × 10^9/L. C-reactive protein is elevated at 85.1 mg/L. Liver function tests show transaminitis indicative of hepatic cytolysis with ALT 112 IU/L and AST 120 IU/L.

Chest radiography demonstrates a systematized heterogeneous opacity in the left medio-thoracic region. Computed tomography (CT) of the chest and abdomen demonstrates osseous lysis of the sternal body with soft tissue infiltration, systematized pulmonary condensation on the left side associated with medio-thoracic mediastinal adenopathies, and splenomegaly with a hypodense intra-splenic lesion.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Bacterial osteomyelitis typically follows an acute, febrile course with local calor, rubor, and rapid purulent collection. In this patient, the lesion evolved indolently over four months in an apyretic state with multifocal pulmonary and splenic involvement. Direct smears of biopsy and respiratory samples were negative for pyogenic organisms, while molecular testing identified mycobacterial DNA.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Bacteriological examination of the surgical sternal biopsy and respiratory specimens did not show acid-fast bacillus on direct examination by Auramine and Ziehl-Neelsen staining, whereas real-time PCR performed with the GeneXpert-Cepheid automated system detected the presence of Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex at very low level without detection of rifampin resistance genes.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Malignant Bone Tumor / Sternal Lymphoma (e.g., Ewing Sarcoma, Osteosarcoma, Hodgkin Lymphoma)
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: The combination of sternal body osteolysis, associated soft-tissue infiltration, mediastinal lymphadenopathy, intrasplenic lesions, and constitutional B-symptoms (weight loss, night sweats) in an adolescent strongly mimics primary bone sarcoma or lymphoma. However, histopathological and microbiological examination confirmed an infectious etiology rather than neoplastic malignancy.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: The computed tomography (CT) scan showed an osseous lysis of the sternal body with infiltration of the soft tissues, a systematized pulmonary condensation on the left side associated with medio-thoracic mediastinal adenopathies and a splenomegaly with a hypodense intra-splenic image

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: The diagnostic pivot occurred when GeneXpert real-time PCR of the surgical sternal biopsy detected Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex at a low level without rifampin resistance, subsequently confirmed by positive cultures on liquid MGIT (6 days) and solid Lowenstein-Jensen media (19 days), establishing multifocal tuberculosis.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: whereas real-time PCR performed with the GeneXpert-Cepheid automated system detected the presence of Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex at very low level without detection of rifampin resistance genes. The GeneXpert is a rapid test that can simultaneously identify M. tuberculosis and detect the resistance to rifampin from sputum... The culture of the biopsy was positive after 6 days on the liquid medium MGIT (mycobacterial growth indicator tube containing 7 ml of modified Middlebrook 7H9 Broth base) (Fig. 3) and 19 days on the solid medium LJ (Lowenstein-Jensen (Fig. 4)).

editor_comments: Admission presentation stops before invasive biopsy and GeneXpert PCR. Redacted disease-identifying references to TB exposure. Differential diagnoses address pyogenic osteomyelitis and chest wall malignancy, with verbatim quotes from the text.
